rules.statement: When a DI-free library meets an open vocabulary, ship the registered members as built-in data and take any other member from the caller as a method or constructor argument; do not add a static mutable registry or a DI service for it.
rules.why: A static mutable registry brings global state with registration-order and test-isolation problems, and a DI service breaks the package's DI-free design.
rules.check: Look in DI-free packages for new static mutable collections or static Register methods used to extend a vocabulary, or for DI service dependencies. The extension point should be an overload or constructor parameter.

rules.statement: Map framework algorithm identifiers to registry names with an explicit table that lists each registry name, and throw NotSupportedException for unmapped values with a message that names the overload that accepts a caller-supplied name; never derive the registry name by rewriting the framework name.
rules.why: Don't infer a trait from a name. An explicit map states each registry name, and an unknown value fails instead of being guessed.
rules.check: Look for string manipulation (ToLower, Replace, etc.) on HashAlgorithmName.Name or similar identifiers to produce protocol names. Also look for a default case that guesses instead of throwing NotSupportedException.

rules.statement: Key lookup tables by HashAlgorithmName with string literals of its Name values, not with `HashAlgorithmName.X.Name`, because `Name` is `string?`.
rules.why: `HashAlgorithmName.Name` is nullable, so using it as a dictionary key brings in nullability problems.
rules.check: Look for dictionary or switch keys written as `HashAlgorithmName.SHA256.Name` or similar.

rules.statement: When a caller supplies a hash name for a JWK Thumbprint URI, require it to match RFC 6920 §3 `1*unreserved` (ASCII letters, digits, `-`, `.`, `_`, `~`), and for a hash the built-in map knows, require the mapped name.
rules.why: This keeps the URN unambiguous, and a known hash can never be mislabeled.
rules.check: Look for overloads that accept a hash or algorithm name and build a URI without validating its characters. Also look for ones that accept a different name for a hash that has a known registry name.

rules.statement: Never produce or map truncated hash registry names (such as `sha-256-128`) for JWK thumbprints; a thumbprint is always the whole digest, and only names of hashes the framework's IncrementalHash computes go in the built-in map.
rules.why: An RFC 7638 thumbprint is the whole digest, and a truncated key identifier weakens the binding.
rules.check: Look for truncated digests, truncated registry names, or map entries for algorithms the framework cannot compute (sha3-224, blake2, k12) in thumbprint code.

rules.statement: Validate a caller-supplied collection of named descriptors as a whole, throwing ArgumentException for a null entry or for two entries with the same name, and match the names with ordinal comparison.
rules.why: The descriptor set is validated as a whole, the same way existing catalogs are, so ambiguous or broken input fails up front.
rules.check: Look for constructors or methods that take descriptor collections without checking for null entries and duplicate names, or that match names with non-ordinal or case-insensitive comparison.

rules.statement: When reading a JWK Set, skip a key whose `kty` is missing, not a string, or empty, using the same test the single-key type applies, so that one malformed key does not make the whole set fail.
rules.why: Otherwise the key reaches a constructor that throws, and the whole set fails, against the intent that one malformed key cannot poison a set.
rules.check: Look for set-parsing loops that construct each key without first applying the key's own validity test, so that one bad member throws and the whole set fails.

rules.statement: Supply type information to a collection when it is constructed or parsed, through constructor and Parse overloads, instead of adding a method that re-types the items after the fact.
rules.why: Re-typing builds each item twice, and a caller can hold an untyped instance by mistake.
rules.check: Look for new methods like `WithKeyTypes(...)` that rebuild an already-parsed collection to attach descriptors.
